title: Accessibility plan addendum and write-off of uncollectible accounts
subtitle: Consent agenda items, accessibility consultation with community groups, and provincial advocacy on AODA requirements
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee met briefly on January 16, 2024. It recommended that Council approve an addendum to the 2023-2027 Multi-Year Accessibility Plan, after the accessibility status report was pulled from the consent agenda for discussion {{vote:m3}}.

The committee also approved the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}. That included a recommendation to write off $31,181.52 in uncollectible accounts receivable for the year ended December 31, 2023. It also included a quarterly summary of tenders, quotations, requests for proposals and consultant selections approved by the Chief Administrative Officer, which was received for information.

During the accessibility discussion, a councillor asked staff to consult a broader range of disability support organizations in future status updates. Staff agreed to look into it. Councillors also discussed how close Ontario is to its 2025 accessibility goal and whether the Region should press the province on the issue. Because these are committee recommendations, Council will consider them at a later meeting. The next committee meeting is February 6, 2024.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the addendum to the 2023-2027 Multi-Year Accessibility Plan, attached as Appendix C to the report {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended writing off $31,181.52 in accounts receivable for the year ended December 31, 2023.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, with the accessibility report removed for separate discussion {{vote:m1}}.

debate: One councillor welcomed the plan's alignment with, and in places its improvement on, provincial accessibility standards. The councillor asked staff to consult more disability support organizations in future updates, beyond the accessibility advisory committee members consulted so far. Staff agreed to take this back.

A councillor asked whether the AODA has compliance timelines and whether the Region is on track. Staff said the province aims for a barrier-free Ontario by 2025. They said most organizations, including the Region, have done substantial work, but it is uncertain whether anyone can fully reach that goal.

A councillor asked about the separate Waterloo Region and Cambridge accessibility advisory committees. Staff said Cambridge chose to form its own committee, and Regional staff consult it on projects specific to Cambridge.

Councillors raised advocacy to the province. One asked whether the Region asks the province for funding or support to meet AODA requirements. Staff said they would check and respond later. Another said more advocacy is needed so municipalities can meet and exceed the standards.
